=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py and workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: the new `_is_heredoc_operator` function (around line 350 in both twin files; `def` line + docstring + single-statement return)
  severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The docstring reads `"""A `<<` or `<<-` heredoc operator; a `<<<` herestring has no heredoc body."""`, but the implementation returns `_is_redirect(token) and token.startswith("<<") and not token.startswith("<<<")`. `_is_redirect` rejects `<<-` because `set("<<-") = {"<", "-"}` is not a subset of `set("<>&") = {"<", ">", "&"}` (`-` is not in the allowed character set). So `_is_heredoc_operator("<<-")` always returns False despite the docstring's claim that `<<-` is supported.
  WHY: No immediate runtime failure today (no caller passes `<<-` tokens through this function, since `_split_redirects` already drops them — the same `set(token) <= set("<>&")` check filters redirect tokens there). The defect is that the docstring, newly introduced by this PR, documents a capability the function does not have. A future maintainer wiring `<<-` handling into `_is_redirect` or `_split_redirects` would then assume `_is_heredoc_operator` counts and binds `<<-` heredoc bodies, when they are silently dropped, triggering the `aligned = sum(counts) == len(bodies)` "bind nothing" fail-safe. The PR description explicitly notes that `<<-` is out of project scope ("Out of project scope and unchanged"), so the docstring overstates what was shipped.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
